summary: Several added comments overstate I/O semantics or omit an interruptible-wait case exposed by their implementations.

items.issue: The field documentation says it controls daemon status for threads running all three handlers, but `Simple.run` always creates the `writeInput` thread as a daemon (`daemon = true`), regardless of this value.
items.suggestion: State that this flag controls the output and error handler threads (and thread builders), or change the implementation if input-handler daemon status is intended to follow it.

items.issue: Call-by-name reevaluates the argument; it does not ensure a newly created stream. Also, the stream is not always closed: `IStreamBuilder` protects the JVM standard input from closing.
items.suggestion: Say that the expression is evaluated on each execution, and that the resulting stream is read and normally closed, except that standard input is protected from closing.

items.issue: The blocking call can throw `InterruptedException` when the caller is interrupted while waiting on the result queue, but the new documentation omits this material outcome.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws InterruptedException` tag describing interruption while waiting for the exit value.

items.issue: The delegated `Future` result function waits with `LinkedBlockingQueue.take`, so this method can throw `InterruptedException` if the caller is interrupted; the documentation promises a result or rethrow of the computation's exception without documenting that case.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws InterruptedException` tag for interruption while waiting for the computation result.

items.issue: The new `!!` and `!` overload documentation states return values in summaries beginning with “Starts”, but omits `@return` tags, contrary to the project convention for descriptions that do not begin with “Returns”.
items.suggestion: Add concise `@return` tags to these overloads, including the exit-code-returning `!` family.

bonus_findings.issue: The pre-existing constructor documentation also incorrectly says `daemonizeThreads` determines the daemon status of the `writeInput` thread; `Simple.run` always makes that thread daemon.
bonus_findings.suggestion: Correct it alongside the new field documentation.

bonus_findings.issue: The pre-existing public API documentation says a call-by-name input stream is recreated and closed for every execution, although reevaluation need not create a distinct stream and standard input is protected from closure.
bonus_findings.suggestion: Align it with the actual reevaluation and standard-input-protection behavior.
